title: 1st Army: feet against rail
summary: The outer wheel was the plan's longest march and its longest supply line. Kluck's corps covered some 500 kilometres in a month on their feet; behind them the railhead crept forward only as the Belgians' demolitions were repaired, and beyond the railhead everything — bread, fodder, shells — came by horse. Herwig and Strachan both put the practical limit of horse-drawn supply at about a hundred kilometres; by the Sambre the 1st Army was past it and by the Marne it was living on the country.[^herwig-2009] [^strachan-2001]

title: 2nd Army: feet against rail
summary: Bülow's line ran through Liège, Namur and Charleroi; Maubeuge, invested but untaken until 7 September, blocked the direct line south and cost the 2nd Army a corps to mask it and a railway to use.[^herwig-2009]
